track_record.note: Surprise->price = directional accuracy among material surprises (|z|>=0.5). Lean = our pre-release bias calling the surprise sign. MAE = avg miss of the model's expected weekly change vs the naive seasonal guess (lower is better).

prediction.headline: Structural lean BULLISH (score +2.53), but the RELEASE itself is a weak same-day catalyst (conditional R²=0.00). Base case: the market is positioned for ~-3.8 MMbbl — the day's move hinges on the surprise vs that, and in this regime inventories are rarely the decisive driver.
factors: U.S. crude stocks are 1.3σ below the 5-year seasonal norm — structurally tight (bullish).
Last 4 weeks averaged a 6.7 MMbbl/week draw — bullish momentum into the print.
Cushing has drawn 5.8 MMbbl over 4 weeks (20.0 MMbbl now) — draining toward tank lows, very bullish for WTI structure.
Seasonally this week normally draws ~5.1 MMbbl (driving season); the model's expected change is -3.8 MMbbl.
Product alignment is 'mixed' — crude and products diverge, so the day-of read is muddier.

Release-day catalyst strength is a weak one: in the current High-vol / Backwardation / driving regime, the crude surprise has historically explained only R²=0.00 of the day's WTI move (n=30) — other drivers (macro, OPEC, positioning) usually dominate the day.

Asymmetry: a sizeable DRAW (~-3.8 MMbbl) is the base case and largely priced, so the bigger surprise risk is a BUILD (bearish). A draw merely in line confirms but adds little; a draw far bigger than -3.8 is the bullish tail.
prediction.narrative: Before the print, the model expects a 4.1 MMbbl draw — that is the number the market is positioned for, so the EXPECTED SURPRISE is ~0 and a print in line should barely move WTI. Our structural lean is BULLISH. Crucially, the release is a weak same-day catalyst here (regime R²=0.01): even a 1σ miss (~5.1 MMbbl) maps to only a small WTI move on the inventory number alone. The real test is whether the print beats or misses that 4.1 MMbbl base case.
